OpenVoiceIME handles dictation alongside your normal typing keyboard. Choose how you want to open it. This guide never changes your default keyboard.
Keep my current keyboard — switch manually
Gboard’s microphone uses Google voice typing and cannot open OpenVoiceIME. You can keep Gboard for typing; opening OpenVoiceIME requires switching keyboards.

Install HeliBoard, then enable it in Android keyboard settings. In HeliBoard Settings → Toolbar → Select pinned toolbar keys, enable Voice input. Its microphone can then open OpenVoiceIME. If another voice keyboard opens, disable that competing voice input in Android keyboard settings. Keep your typing keyboard enabled. No additional app store is required.
HeliBoard settings are unavailable. Install HeliBoard first, then return here. You can enable it in Android keyboard settings below.
HeliBoard settings are available. Enable HeliBoard in Android keyboard settings and pin Voice input in its toolbar.

Keep your normal keyboard enabled. Use Android’s keyboard icon or Change keyboard notification to select OpenVoiceIME when dictating. Some phones hide auxiliary voice keyboards, so OpenVoiceIME may be missing even when enabled. If it is missing, use the HeliBoard route. Changing the system speech-recognition engine does not redirect Gboard’s microphone.

Tap the test field, then use the keyboard picker or HeliBoard microphone. Dictate and tap Stop. Use Return to normal keyboard afterward. Automatic return follows Android’s keyboard order when several keyboards are enabled.
Dictation also needs a working transcription endpoint and token. Configure and test them in Server below. Test text is not saved as a setting.

Ctrl+Shift+Space opens dictation. Ctrl+Shift+Enter transcribes, inserts, and hides the panel without switching keyboards. Filters these shortcuts; does not read screen content or save typed text. Enable OpenVoiceIME as a keyboard first. Requires Android 11 or newer.

Enable OpenVoiceIME keyboard shortcut in Android Accessibility settings. Keep your virtual keyboard hidden and focus a text field. Ctrl+Shift+Space opens recording; Ctrl+Shift+Enter transcribes, inserts, and hides the panel without switching keyboards or sending Enter to the app. Errors keep the panel open; press the finish shortcut again to retry. Confirmation is skipped for this action only. The optional service does not read screen content or save typed text.
Shortcut service enabled: Ctrl+Shift+Space to record; Ctrl+Shift+Enter to insert and hide.
Shortcut service disabled. Enable it in Android Accessibility settings.
The global shortcut requires Android 11 or newer.

Optional shortcut for WhatsApp and Telegram: select one voice message and tap the floating Transcribe button. This service reads visible interface controls to operate More, Share and the OpenVoiceIME destination. It does not store chat screen contents. Only the audio you explicitly share is sent to your configured provider. Disable this service to remove the shortcut.

WhatsApp / Telegram: hold one voice message, then tap the floating Transcribe button. Enable the optional message transcription accessibility service below. It needs access to visible screen controls to handle the Share menus. Audio goes to the same provider configured here; no microphone permission or keyboard activation is needed. Menu automation currently recognizes English and Spanish controls and may need updates for your app version. If the button is missing or sharing fails, use the message menu → Share → Transcribe audio · OpenVoiceIME.
